subject: Post-demo: Healthlytics fit + evaluation roadmap and tool-calling notes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthlytics.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Healthlytics fit + evaluation roadmap and tool-calling notes

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so your team can kick off the evaluation without a hitch.

Recap (2 min):
- Primary goal: automated extraction of clinical visit summaries + structured claims flags (JSON output) for downstream ingestion into EHR and billing.
- Volume estimate: 120k docs/month, 95% single-session summaries, 5% multi-document aggregation.
- Key constraints: PII handling, <300ms p95 latency target for real-time preview, strict schema validation on output.

Recommended immediate steps (we propose):
1) Evaluation bundle (7–10 days):
   - Two model variants to test: redwood-2.7b-std (fast baseline) and redwood-13b-sparse (higher-fidelity structured output).
   - Pre-built prompt set + 60 representative records (you to upload redacted sample) — link to prompt sets: https://redwood-inference.shared.drive/HLX/eval-prompt-sets
   - Metrics: schema-compliance rate (JSON-valid), field-level precision/recall on key entities, hallucination rate (false-positive flags).
2) Tool/function calling prototype:
   - We'll provide a JSON Schema and function-call wrapper for the three output objects (visit_summary, diagnosis_flags, billing_codes). See attached json-schema-example.json for the baseline.
   - Retry semantics: idempotent retries for transient timeouts (exponential backoff, max 3 retries). We will include a small harness that demonstrates the retry policy and how KV caching reduces duplicate token cost.
3) Benchmarks:
   - We’ll run the same 60-record set across the two model variants and provide latency/cost/quality tradeoff report (link to benchmark stub: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/hlx-2027-report).
4) Compliance & data flow:
   - For PII controls we recommend Dedicated or Private deploy (we outlined options in the doc attached).

Immediate asks from you:
- Confirm availability of a redacted 60-record sample by next Tue (2027-07-20).
- Confirm whether procurement wants an SOW or a PO first.

Attaching: healthlytics-demo-notes.pdf (demo recording + transcript), proposed-eval-plan.xlsx (timeline & milestones), json-schema-example.json (sample output schema).

If you’re good with the plan I’ll loop in Rishi for the eval setup and Dylan for post-eval CS/ops readiness.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Great questions — looping in Rishi (solutions) and Dylan (Customer Ops) to pick up technical/compliance items. High level answers below and then Rishi will propose the eval config.

Samir / Lina — quick answers:
- Eval location: we can run the evaluation in three ways (in order of preference for minimal data movement):
  1) Your GCP project using Redwood Private eval agent (we provide an image + orchestration that runs inside the VPC).
  2) Dedicated tenant in Redwood in the same cloud region with strict transient storage and audit logs.
  3) Hosted Redwood API with encrypted uploads and short-lived tokens (least preferred for PII).
- Optional/unknown fields: recommended contract is "explicit schema + enums + open_attributes map" pattern. In practice we validate required fields strictly and return an open_map field for any ancillary attributes with a clear annotation (source_confidence). That preserves backwards compatibility for downstream. See attached json-schema-example.json; Rishi — please highlight the required vs optional fields and the open_map pattern in the eval harness.
- SOW: I’ll draft a one-pager and attach within the hour.

Rishi / Dylan — can you own:
  - Rishi: eval harness (model variants, prompt set, schema validation runner, example scoring notebook).
  - Dylan: intake for procurement + draft SOW + production handoff checklist (SLA/latency, fallback policies, rollout plan).

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Samir — thanks, and great to meet you all. I’m Rishi, Solutions Engineer — short plan below and two small asks so we can start tomorrow if you confirm.

Concrete eval plan (timeline: 7 business days):
- Day 0: ingestion & redaction check (we’ll run a quick script to verify de-identification labels).
- Day 1–2: run both models (redwood-2.7b-std + redwood-13b-sparse) across 60-record set with default prompt templates.
- Day 3: schema compliance pass (JSON Schema validator), field-level extraction scoring, and a hallucination spot-check (10 random records).
- Day 4: run tool/function-calling variant where model returns function-call for the structured objects; compare to direct JSON output (this helps isolate function-calling determinism).
- Day 5: cost/latency benchmarking + produce a short report and recommendations.

Model recommendations rationale:
- redwood-2.7b-std: preferred for latency-sensitive pathways (preview UI), expect p95 < 250ms on Dedicated with batching disabled for real-time.
- redwood-13b-sparse: higher accuracy on nested fields and rare codes; recommended for nightly batch enrichment and final billing extraction.

Function-calling & retries:
- We’ll test function-call mode with the JSON Schema as the function signature. For retries we recommend: idempotent retry up to 3 attempts for transient network errors or server 5xx, and a deterministic checksum on inputs to detect duplicates. The eval harness will log per-request attempt ids and outcomes so you can measure cost impact of retries.

Schema contract (excerpt):
- visit_summary: { required: visit_id, clinician_id, summary_text }
- diagnosis_flags: { array of {code, confidence, onset_date? } }
- billing_codes: { array of strings }
- open_map: { arbitrary key-values, each with source_confidence percent }

Two small asks:
1) Confirm which eval environment you prefer (GCP VPC agent vs Redwood Dedicated).
2) Drop the 60 de-identified records in the secure upload link I’ll share (expires in 72 hrs).

I’ll upload the small notebook and the JSON schema validator script to the shared drive in the next hour.

—Rishi
